result:
Note: this `workspace` directory isn't actually under git version control (it's gitignored scratch output in the outer harness repo), so there's nothing to commit — these are just plain file edits in place.

**Summary of changes made to the Lumina codebase:**

1. **`app/layout.tsx`** — replaced the stale "InboxZap — Clean Your Inbox in Minutes" default title/description/OG tags with correct Lumina branding, and added sitewide `Organization` JSON-LD.
2. **`app/page.tsx`** — added its own metadata/canonical, `SoftwareApplication` JSON-LD, a real `#faq` section (fixing the dead `/faq → /#faq` redirect) with an explicit **"Is Lumina the same as InboxZap?"** FAQ entry to catch confused branded searchers, `FAQPage` JSON-LD, and internal links to 3 new blog posts.
3. **`app/blog/posts.ts`** (new) — 5 new, substantive posts: one explaining the InboxZap→Lumina rebrand (to capture that branded-search traffic), and four targeting real meeting-productivity keywords (AI meeting notes, writing meeting minutes, action items, async standups).
4. **`app/blog/page.tsx`** — rebuilt as a server component (was `'use client'` fetching a nonexistent `/api/posts`, so it showed "Loading posts…" forever to users and crawlers alike). Now renders real, crawlable links with proper metadata.
5. **`app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx`** (new) — statically generated post pages with per-post metadata, canonical URLs, and `BlogPosting` JSON-LD.
6. **`app/sitemap.ts`** — now includes all 5 new posts (previously explicitly TODO'd out).
7. **`next.config.js`** — added 301s from the 12 orphaned legacy `/blog/post-N` URLs (all old email-cleanup content, irrelevant to the current product) to `/blog`, retiring thin/off-topic pages that were burning crawl budget for zero clicks.

Verified with a full `next build` + `next start`: build succeeds, all new post pages prerender, the legacy redirects and `/faq` redirect both fire correctly, and all three JSON-LD blocks render on the homepage.

One thing outside my ability to fix: the OG image path (`/img/og-lumina.png`) referenced in metadata doesn't correspond to an actual file in `public/` — worth uploading a real image there, since broken social preview images hurt share CTR.
